# Sequences

<!-- purpose: Where Sequences files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Sequence scenarios, one task each; each is drawn as a sequence diagram whose files are named from the scenario's name.

One file per `sequence`, in `sequences/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

## `sequence` { #sequence }

<!-- purpose: Writing `sequence` files in Sequences: each key, its type and default -->

One sequence scenario: an ordered walk through some of the runnables of exactly one task, drawn as a sequence diagram. The steps must follow the task's own runnable order.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The scenario's identity, which also names its sequence diagram's files. Must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ — a rule of this layer alone, deliberately not the AUTOSAR `Identifier` rule. |
| `task` | string, the `name` of [tasks](tasks.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared task this scenario walks; exactly one per scenario, and every step must be mapped to it. |
| `title` | string | no | `""` | The scenario's human-readable title, shown after its name in the heading of its sequence diagram (`sd {name} — {title}`). When empty, the heading is the name alone. |
| `steps` | a list of `sequence_step` blocks | yes | — | The steps of the scenario, in order. Must not be empty and must be an ordered subsequence of the referenced task's runnables. |

## Blocks used inside those files { #blocks-used-inside-those-files }

<!-- purpose: The blocks nested inside Sequences files, which are not files of their own -->

These are not files of their own: each appears as a block inside an element of this layer.

### `sequence_step` { #sequence_step }

<!-- purpose: Writing `sequence_step` blocks in Sequences: each key, its type and default -->

One step of a sequence scenario: the runnable it shows, its component named by exactly one of `swc` and `instance`, with an optional note. The `(swc, instance, runnable)` triple, the absent selector as `null`, is the step's identity; the step must be mapped to the scenario's task, and a step written the same way appears at most once per scenario.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `swc` | string, the `name` of [swc](swc.md) | no | absent | The name of the declared software component the step runs in; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable. |
| `instance` | string | no | absent | The occurrence of a component below the root composition the step runs in, as a `/`-joined path of composition member names from the root composition down — a member of the root is its member name alone, a nested one `outer/inner` — never starting with the root composition's own name; exactly one of `swc` and `instance` is set. Part of the step's composite identity, and so immutable. |
| `runnable` | string | yes | — | The name of a runnable of that component, which must be mapped to the scenario's task. Part of the composite identity, and so immutable. |
| `note` | string | no | `""` | Free text shown beside the step on its sequence diagram; when non-empty the step's activation is labelled `{runnable} — {note}`. |
